component.name: OpenCIE
component.summary: Sign documents with the Italian CIE

description.p: OpenCIE is an open-source application for digital signatures, verification, and identity management with the Italian Electronic Identity Card (CIE — Carta d'Identità Elettronica).

ul.li: Sign — CAdES (.p7m), PAdES (PDF), and XAdES (.xml) digital signatures using the CIE chip
Verify — validate signatures with OCSP/CRL revocation checking
Manage — enroll and manage CIE cards, change or unblock the PIN

description.p: A PC/SC-compatible smart card or contactless reader is required to communicate with the card.

screenshot.caption: Sign documents with the CIE chip

description.p: Linux on ARM and a refreshed look, with native library opencie-pkcs11 1.2.1.

ul.li: New Linux arm64 builds: tarball and Flatpak.
Optional update check: a once-a-day notice when a new release is out (can be turned off in Settings).
Refreshed app icon.
Updated PoDoFo, pcsc-lite and other bundled dependencies.

description.p: Broader card support, with native library opencie-pkcs11 1.2.0.

ul.li: Newer CIE chips (Actalis B946) are recognised, and future Actalis/Bit4id revisions are handled automatically.
Unsupported chips get a clear message explaining how to report them, instead of "not a CIE".
Readers with several slots show the slot holding the card or the contactless one.
Flatpak: logs and card cache now persist across restarts.

description.p: Reliable card reading, with native library opencie-pkcs11 1.1.4.

ul.li: Contactless readers and phone NFC recover from brief card movements, without ever costing a PIN attempt.
Missing photo or MRZ data is reported with Retry and Continue, and can be read later from the card page.
Android enrolment now reads the chip, including the photo.
Fixed timestamps occasionally rejected and a possible hang in desktop sign-in.

description.p: Signing, verification and Android fixes, with native library opencie-pkcs11 1.1.3.

ul.li: Android NFC can reach the card again, and signing sends the full 8-digit PIN correctly.
Verifying a signed document no longer crashes, and OCSP/CRL revocation checks work for CIE signatures.
Desktop-to-phone signing now signs the actual document instead of its digest.
Enrolled cards show their certificate dates, serial and last use; re-enrolling updates the card instead of duplicating it.
Clearer card errors, an in-dialog shortcut when NFC is off, and live PIN feedback.
Long-term validation fixes: OCSP parsing, timestamp checks, already-signed PDFs and archive timestamps.
Works without a running keyring; TSA and proxy passwords moved to secure storage.
Android releases are release-signed, per-architecture APKs.
The Windows installer now ships the runtime libraries the PKCS#11 module links against; they were silently omitted from every previous installer.
Prebuilt native libraries are verified against the upstream SHA256 checksums before they are packaged.
Signing now hashes with raw digest octets, fixing signatures produced through the signing SDK.
Unsupported hash mechanisms are rejected instead of signing invalid data.
Audit hardening in the native library: signature verification, ASN.1 memory safety, leaks and races.
The macOS build now bundles every library the PKCS#11 module needs and requests the smartcard entitlement, so card readers are detected.
Quitting the app no longer hangs until the USB reader is unplugged.
Settings shows the real application version instead of a hardcoded one.

description.p: Signature placement and OpenID Connect hardening.

ul.li: Signatures are aligned to existing PDF form fields, and weak PINs are rejected.
OpenID Connect discovery now validates the issuer, requires HTTPS and pins the endpoint origin.

description.p: Corrects the Windows installer, which was labelled with the previous version number.

ul.li: Fixed PIN entry on the signing screens, which capped input at 4 digits while the CIE PIN is 8.
Tokens and enrolled-card records are now stored encrypted in the system keyring instead of plain text.
Repeated wrong PIN entries are throttled, and PIN screens block screenshots and screen recording on Android.
Card failures now explain what went wrong and how to recover, instead of a generic error.
Card reading is announced to screen readers, and animations honour the reduced-motion setting.
Expired sign-in sessions are renewed silently instead of forcing a new login.

description.p: Initial release: CAdES/PAdES/XAdES signing, signature verification with OCSP/CRL, CIE card management.
